data.body_html:
October is Marbella's best-kept secret for boating. The summer heat fades, the sea stays warm at 22°C, and the marina at Puerto Banús loses its chaos. With 8 hours of daylight and average winds of 12–21 kn, you get ideal conditions for a relaxed charter — without the July crowds or the winter chill. Here's what to expect from Marbella boat rental weather in October, plus which boats and routes make the most of the shoulder season.

Why October is the smart month for a boat rental in Marbella

October offers the sweet spot between summer and winter. Air temperatures hover around 24°C, sea water stays at 22°C, and the sun is still strong enough for swimming. The key difference? You'll share the anchorages with a handful of boats, not a flotilla. Puerto Banús is quieter, and you can often book your preferred time slot at short notice.

Rain is rare — typically 4–5 days across the month, and usually a short shower. The prevailing winds are light to moderate, with afternoon breezes of 12–21 kn that keep things fresh but not rough. For a full-day trip, you can comfortably cover 30–40 NM and still be back for sunset.

October sea conditions: what to expect on the water

The Mediterranean off Marbella is calm in October. Swell heights average 0.5–1 m, and the sea state is generally smooth to slight. The wind picks up around 14:00, so morning departures are calmest. If you're heading east towards Cala Cortés, you'll get shelter from the Sierra Blanca; west towards Estepona, the coast is more exposed but still manageable.

Water visibility improves after summer — expect 15–20 m — making it a great month for snorkelling. The sea temperature of 22°C is comfortable for swimming without a wetsuit, though a thin one adds comfort for longer dips. Here's a quick snapshot:

Best boats for October charters from Puerto Banús

For a couple or small group, the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) or Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) are perfect — both at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, with skipper, drinks, and snacks included. These flybridges offer an enclosed saloon if the wind picks up, plus a sundeck for those sunny October afternoons.

If you're celebrating or want extra space, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is our flagship — from €4,719 for 4 hours, including a jet ski. Its high bow handles any chop with ease, and the large aft deck is ideal for lounging. For other boats like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86, pricing is on request via WhatsApp — we'll tailor a quote to your needs.

Top October routes: from Puerto Banús to Cabopino and Estepona

October's mild conditions open up a range of routes. Here are three favourites:

  • Cala del Faro (1.5 NM west) — Sheltered cove, clear water, and a beach club that's quieter in October.
  • Cala Cortés (3 NM east) — A rocky inlet with excellent snorkelling and a backdrop of the Sierra Blanca.
  • Estepona (12 NM west) — A longer cruise past San Pedro and the Río Verde; anchor off the old town for lunch.

For a full-day trip, combine Cala Cortés with a stop at Cabopino (6 NM east) — the marina there has a laid-back vibe, and the dunes are worth a walk. All routes are easily covered within 4–8 hours, depending on your pace.

What's included in your October charter

Every charter from our fleet includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden extras. In October, we also provide a light jacket on board for evening returns, and you can request snorkelling gear at no extra cost.

For the full experience, we recommend a 4-hour morning charter (10:00–14:00) to catch the calmest seas and the best light. Or go for a 2-hour sunset cruise (17:00–19:00) — the autumn sunsets over La Concha are spectacular.

Booking tips for October: availability and pricing

October is shoulder season, but it's still wise to book 3–5 days in advance, especially for weekends. You'll have more choice of boats and time slots. Prices are the same as summer for our Tier A boats (€749/2h), but you get more value because the experience is more intimate — fewer boats at anchor, warmer service, and no queues at Puerto Banús.

For larger groups (up to 12 pax), the Mangusta 80 at €4,719 for 4 hours is a standout deal, as it includes a jet ski. If you're flexible, ask about last-minute specials — we sometimes have openings midweek at reduced rates.

Safety and weather: what if the sea turns rough?

October is generally calm, but we keep a close eye on forecasts. If winds are forecast above 25 kn or there's a yellow alert, we'll suggest a route change or reschedule your charter free of charge. Our skippers are local and know the sheltered spots along the coast, so you're always in safe hands.

We also recommend booking a morning slot in October, as afternoon breezes can freshen. If you're prone to seasickness, pick a boat with a stabiliser system (like the Mangusta 80) or stick to the leeward side of the coast.
